title: My mobile hero RPG is live: 15 lands, 15 bosses, every picture made with the GPT image model. This hit does 9.2 billion damage.
author: KasperzackGames
selftext:
Reelguard is a mobile hero RPG where each hero's attack is a reel: line up swords, fireballs, shields and hearts and the party strikes. It went live on Google Play on 26 Nov. I wrote the code in Godot, with Claude Code as my coding assistant. The art comes from the GPT image model: heroes, monsters, backgrounds and UI pieces, and every prompt carries the same look-target picture so the style stays consistent.



Hands were the hardest part. My prompts said "every visible hand with a thumb and four fingers", and fists still came back with three fingers or as mitten-like blobs. Re-rolling the whole hero wasn't an option: it would break the match with that hero's other gear looks and poses.



So only the hand gets repainted:



1. Crop the hand and enlarge it to 1024 px.

2. Send it to the image model with the whole picture as reference, and a prompt that says what is wrong and what must stay.

3. Paste it back with a script that lines it up and keeps only the pixels that changed round the hand.

4. Check every hand at 4x, finger by finger.



In one pass that was 637 hero pictures and 132 fixed hands.



My part: I designed and programmed the game with Claude Code helping, reviewed every change, played the builds on my phone and reported what was wrong (the first ranger hand that was a finger short included), and approved the pictures that set the bar for the rest.



The video is recorded gameplay with the game's own sounds; the music is CC0. Gear from chests climbs up to Celestial, which is how a hit goes from 110 million to the 9.2 billion at the start.



It's free on Google Play (Android), with ads and optional purchases: [https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.kasperzackgames.reelguard](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.kasperzackgames.reelguard)



How do you handle hands: a repair pass like this, or regenerate until it's right?
